judged_text: The Salesforce CalendarService constructor now performs an unconditional eager token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com on every instantiation, replacing the previous jsforce-managed refresh flow; this work is not traceable to the stated 'credential sync' intent and runs even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false. Every Salesforce calendar operation now adds a blocking network round-trip (and a DB write) on the hot path even for standard self-hosted installs with no credential sharing configured; a Salesforce outage or 429 on the token endpoint now fails calendar reads/writes that previously used the cached access token via jsforce.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor (or initialization path) now unconditionally performs a refresh-token `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (see the newly added block starting around `const response = await fetch(...)`). This runs regardless of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (no guard around the fetch/update), adding a blocking network round-trip and DB write on each instantiation and making all Salesforce calendar operations fail if the token endpoint is down/returns non-OK (it throws on `response.statusText !== "OK"`). Those behaviors are directly verifiable from the diff and can regress reliability/performance even when credential sharing is not configured.
